newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ yields end sharply higher after U.S. rate hike.
newsitem.headline: NZ yields end sharply higher after U.S. rate hike.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close

OVERNIGHT CASH 7.50 PCT (PREV 7.50) US 5-YR 6.66 (PREV 6.57)
* NZ yields end sharply higher after U.S. rate hike
* Global trends overshadowing local situation
* Traders wary of conditions being overly tight
New Zealand's debt market was stung by the adverse reaction in the U.S. to the expected quarter point rate rise and sold off sharply on Wednesday.
Dealers said that although monetary conditions in New Zealand were now 40 basis points tighter than the Reserve Bank has indicated is desirable, global trends were overriding local factors.
Bond dealers said they expect further weakness in the U.S. as traders anticipate further rate hikes in the U.S.
"If the U.S. does weaken, we will probably sell off," he said.
New Zealand long bond yields rose around 12 basis points, performing much worse than other dollar bloc countries, especially Australia.
"There's no clear reason why," he said.
Bills were also sold heavily with the June futures ending at 92.16 against the 92.29 session high. Volume was 3144.
A bill dealer described today's reaction as "peculiar".
"The Reserve Bank must be wondering what's going on," he said.
He doubted bill yields would rise much higher while the Trade-Weighted Index remained at its current high level.

He suggested the Reserve Bank may be prompted to comment if conditions remain overly tight for too much more. ------------------------(SPREADS)------------------------------ NZD VS 3 YR 10 YR * NZD 3-YR/10-YR SPREAD
